current_product_snapshot.title: Quiet Control Companion
current_product_snapshot.silhouette: low-profile rounded dorsal-wrist pod with no snagging protrusions
current_product_snapshot.body_placement: dorsal wrist, centered proximal to wrist crease
current_product_snapshot.attachment_strategy: broad vented strap with keyed clasp and intentional quick release
current_product_snapshot.contact_area: broad compliant underside, avoiding wrist prominences
current_product_snapshot.mass_distribution: centered over wrist/forearm axis with no distal overhang
current_product_snapshot.feedback_timing: bounded pulse at a safe task boundary
current_product_snapshot.visible_state: wearer-facing state edge shows active/sensing state without content
current_product_snapshot.cancel_action: guarded recessed one-handed press-hold; no response terminates routine event

scenario_state_machine.name: Crowded transit routine intervention
scenario_state_machine.purpose: Suppress routine AI intervention during movement hazards while preserving a bounded, private recovery path.

transitions.guard: doors, stairs, crossing or high-motion transit is declared
transitions.user_control_boundary: movement state does not imply intent, consent or attention

transitions.action: record only minimal event metadata and defer
transitions.user_control_boundary: no public output and no escalation

transitions.guard: hazard no longer declared and intervention permission remains valid
transitions.user_control_boundary: safe boundary is not consent; user may still reject or ignore
no visual or two-handed response is required

transitions.action: stop event and suppress ordinary re-intervention in scope
terminate with no implicit consent and no escalation
stop current event and require new permission decision

transitions.guard: new permission and no active hazard
transitions.user_control_boundary: previous response is not generalized beyond scope

invariants: Routine intervention never uses public audio for private content.
No-response ends a routine event; it never grants consent.
Hazard, pose, route and movement state are context inputs, not evidence of intent or emotion.
Rejection and correction do not trigger ordinary escalation.
When hands are unavailable, the system relies on suppression or timeout rather than pretending a physical control is reachable.

prototype_validation_protocol.title: Transit Anchor physical prototype validation
prototype_validation_protocol.objective: Test whether the declared wrist form preserves bounded control and low interruption under plausible crowded-transit movement conditions.
prototype_validation_protocol.prototype_boundary: This is a test plan, not evidence that a render, CAD blockout or design declaration meets any target.
prototype_validation_protocol.participants_and_context: Consented adult participants perform controlled standing-transit, handrail, bag-carrying, sleeve and walking tasks; no road-crossing or live transit hazard is required for the first protocol.

measures.question: Does the device slip or rotate under declared movements?
measures.metric: displacement and rotation relative to initial marked position
measures.acceptance_boundary: Pre-register a tolerable displacement/rotation threshold before data collection; do not derive it from the render.

measures.question: Does gripping or incidental contact trigger guarded controls?
measures.metric: false activations per task and per controlled exposure time
measures.acceptance_boundary: Compare against a pre-registered maximum false-activation rate.

measures.question: Can a reachable user perform reject/stop without visual search?
measures.metric: completion rate, completion time and erroneous activation
measures.acceptance_boundary: Pre-register success and time bounds; hands-unavailable trials test suppression/timeout policy rather than control reachability.

measures.question: Is the private haptic pattern detectable without demanding visual attention?
measures.metric: hit rate, false alarm rate and response time
measures.acceptance_boundary: Pre-register a detection criterion and distinguish non-detection from rejection.

measures.question: Does the declared contact geometry create observable pressure, heat or irritation signals in the short protocol?
measures.metric: participant-reported discomfort plus measured surface/skin-adjacent temperature where safely instrumented
measures.acceptance_boundary: Exploratory safety screen only until duration, measurement method and threshold are pre-registered.

measures.question: Can bystanders infer private content from routine feedback?
measures.metric: observer identification of state versus private content
measures.acceptance_boundary: Pre-register acceptable content-identification rate; state-legibility and content leakage are analyzed separately.

stopping_conditions: Stop an individual session on discomfort, skin irritation, distress or a participant request.
Do not test the routine intervention flow in live road-crossing, vehicle-door or stair hazards in this first protocol.
Pause the protocol if a control failure removes the local stop path.
outcomes_not_claimed: user intent, emotion or consent inference

portfolio_boundary: This portfolio projection separates declared design changes, derived graphics and planned validation. It never presents Blender output or scenario context as proof of user outcomes, comfort, consent, engineering readiness or physical performance.
